g.text: Three ways of choosing sample sites in one area
Selection procedures (first define the eligible frame)
Random (A): number every eligible site, then choose by chance,
e.g. a random-number table, without replacement. Here sites 3, 8,
Systematic (B): state the start and the fixed interval, here 0 m
and every 10 m, then sample each point the rule gives: 11 points
Stratified (C): define the two zones first, then apply a rule
within each zone (here a chance draw of three) so both zones are
covered. Record the sites chosen, any safe replacements and the
Beach survey: stations and record sheet
Sea: no entry into the water
safe route along the upper beach
Pebble = longest dimension, in mm; mean in mm.
Fall = drop in cm over a 10 m horizontal run at each station.
A and C completed (j); B is the calculation in (d).
Tourism survey: respondent form and tally
Respondent form (one per person; no names recorded)
Read exactly as written: “Has tourism here brought you
the benefit named on this card?”
Refusals and non-response: record separately, not as “no”.
